data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

extract_result.subject: USDA Classified National Security Information Program
extract_result.opi: Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Coordination

supersedes.document_title: USDA Classified National Security Information Program Manual

extract_result.purpose: This Departmental Manual (DM) establishes the policies and procedures that govern the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Classified National Security Information (CNSI) Program, including uniform requirements and guidance for classifying, safeguarding, declassifying, and destroying CNSI, whether originated by or released to USDA. It also prescribes the procedures, requirements, restrictions, and other safeguards to protect special classes of CNSI, including Restricted Data (RD), Formerly Restricted Data (FRD), intelligence sources and methods information, Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), and Special Access Program (SAP) information.
extract_result.scope: This DM applies to all USDA Mission Areas, Agencies, Offices, employees and contractors who possess, handle, distribute, process, transmit, transport, store, and/or who have been entrusted with CNSI and are required to protect that information according to standards commensurate with those discussed in this DM.

All persons who enter or exit a SWA
SSO, ISC’s, and SSC’s responsible for accredited SWAs
ISC’s and SSC’s responsible for accredited SWAs
Designated cleared employees as couriers, hand carriers, and escorts

Director, Office of Human Resource Management (OHRM)

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Manual (DM) establishes the policies and procedures that govern the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Classified National Security Information (CNSI) Program, including uniform requirements and guidance for classifying, safeguarding, declassifying, and destroying CNSI, whether originated by or released to USDA.

It also prescribes the procedures, requirements, restrictions, and other safeguards to protect special classes of CNSI, including Restricted Data (RD), Formerly Restricted Data (FRD), intelligence sources and methods information, Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI), and Special Access Program (SAP) information.
policy_statements.target: special classes of CNSI, including Restricted Data (RD), Formerly Restricted Data (FRD), intelligence sources and methods information, Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI)

policy_statements.source_text: This DM applies to all USDA Mission Areas, Agencies, Offices, employees and contractors who possess, handle, distribute, process, transmit, transport, store, and/or who have been entrusted with CNSI and are required to protect that information according to standards commensurate with those discussed in this DM.
policy_statements.target: USDA Mission Areas, Agencies, Offices, employees and contractors

policy_statements.source_text: This DM implements applicable Federal statutes, Executive Orders (E.O.), national directives, international treaties, and certain Government-to-Government agreements.

The authority for this guidance is derived from E.O. 13526, Classified National Security Information; E.O. 13587, Structural Reforms to Improve the Security of Classified Networks and the Responsible Sharing and Safeguarding of Classified Information; 32 Code of Federal Regulation (CFR) Part 2001, Classified National Security Information, Final Rule; Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-11-08, Initial Assessment of Safeguarding and Counterintelligence Postures for Classified National Security Information in Automated Systems; and, Departmental Regulation (DR) 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Regulation.
cross_references: E.O. 13587, Structural Reforms to Improve the Security of Classified Networks and the Responsible Sharing and Safeguarding of Classified Information
32 Code of Federal Regulation (CFR) Part 2001, Classified National Security Information, Final Rule
M-11-08, Initial Assessment of Safeguarding and Counterintelligence Postures for Classified National Security Information in Automated Systems
(DR) 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Regulation

policy_statements.source_text: This DM supersedes DM 3440-001, USDA Classified National Security Information Program Manual, dated May 1, 2008.
E.O. 13526 requires each Department that has been given Original Classification Authority (OCA) to establish a CNSI program that ensures the protection of CNSI.
policy_statements.target: CNSI program that ensures the protection of CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: The Secretary of Agriculture is responsible for originally classifying USDA information, up to the Secret level, the unauthorized disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to cause serious damage to the national security.
policy_statements.target: USDA information, up to the Secret level, the unauthorized disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to cause serious damage to the national security

policy_statements.source_text: In addition, the Secretary will:
Demonstrate a personal commitment and commit senior management to the successful implementation of the CNSI program;
Commit necessary resources to the effective implementation of the CNSI program established;

Ensure that Departmental record systems are designed and maintained to optimize the appropriate sharing of CNSI, and to facilitate its declassification under the terms of E.O. 13526 when it no longer meets the standards for continued classification;
Receive specific training on how to originally classify USDA information; and
policy_statements.target: specific training on how to originally classify USDA information

policy_statements.source_text: Designate a Senior Agency Official (SAO) to direct and administer the CNSI program.

The Assistant Secretary for Administration (ASA) is designated by the Secretary as the SAO who oversees the CNSI program and serves as liaison between USDA and the National Archives and Records Administration (NARA), Information Security Oversight Office (ISOO).
policy_statements.target: USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This designation has been re-delegated to the Director of USDA’s Office of Homeland Security and Emergency Coordination (OHSEC).
The SAO shall maintain eligibility for access to CNSI commensurate to the level of information held or handled within the agency and will:
policy_statements.target: eligibility for access to CNSI commensurate to the level of information held or handled within the agency and will

policy_statements.source_text: Oversee USDA’s CNSI program;
policy_statements.target: USDA’s CNSI program

policy_statements.source_text: Promulgate implementing regulations, which shall be published in the Federal Register to the extent that they affect members of the public;
Ensure that there are Security Education, Training, and Awareness (SETA) programs, and establish the training schedule;

Ensure that there is an ongoing self-inspection program, which shall include, but is not limited to, regular reviews of representative samples of the agency’s original and derivative classification actions, and shall authorize appropriate agency officials to correct misclassification actions not covered by Section 1.7(c) and 1.7(d) of E.O. 13526, and ensure delegate reports annually to the Director of ISOO on the agency’s self-inspection program;
Establish procedures consistent with directives issued pursuant to E.O. 13526 to prevent unnecessary access to CNSI;
policy_statements.target: procedures consistent with directives issued pursuant to E

policy_statements.source_text: Require that a need for access to classified information be established before initiating administrative clearance procedures; and
Ensure that that the number of persons granted access to classified information meets the mission needs of the agency while also satisfying operational and security requirements and needs.
Develop special contingency plans for the safeguarding of CNSI used in or near high risk environments;
policy_statements.target: of CNSI used in or near high risk environments

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that the performance evaluation used to rate employee performance includes the designation and management of CNSI as a critical element or item to be evaluated in the rating of:
Original classification authorities;
Security managers or security specialists; and
All other personnel whose duties significantly involve the creation or handling of classified information, including personnel who regularly apply derivative classification markings.
Account for the costs associated with the implementation of this DM, which shall be reported to the Director of ISOO for publication;

Assign in a prompt manner agency personnel to any request, appeal, challenge, complaint, or suggestion arising out of this DM that pertains to CNSI that originated in a component of the Department that no longer exists and for which there is no clear successor in function;
Report annually to ISOO as required by 32 CFR Part 2001, and have the SAO sign and review all outgoing reports; and
policy_statements.target: annually to ISOO as required by 32 CFR Part 2001

policy_statements.source_text: Establishing a secure capability to receive information, allegations, or complaints regarding over-classification or incorrect classification within the agency and to provide guidance to personnel on proper classification as needed.
policy_statements.target: information, allegations

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices are responsible for:
Collaborating with OHSEC to incorporate language defining security duties and responsibilities and qualifications for position descriptions and performance elements;
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices

policy_statements.source_text: Identifying to OHSEC an Information Security Coordinator (ISC); and
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices

policy_statements.source_text: Identifying to OHSEC a Top Secret Control Officer (TSCO).
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices

policy_statements.source_text: The TSCO can also serve as the ISC.
The TSCO will be approved and appointed in writing by the Agency Head.
The Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD) of OHSEC, is responsible for revisions, additions, or deletions to this document.
policy_statements.actor_name: Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD) of OHSEC

policy_statements.source_text: In addition, PDSD will:
Serve as the Special Security Office (SSO) for the department.
policy_statements.target: department

policy_statements.source_text: The SSO is responsible for the day-to-day security management and implementation of the department’s CNSI program.
This includes, but is not limited to:
Establish and maintain SETA programs to include training the OCA;

Collaborate with USDA Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices to incorporate language defining security duties and responsibilities and qualifications for position descriptions and performance elements for the ISC, Site Security Coordinator (SSC) and TSCO;
Establish and maintain a self-inspection program, which shall include the periodic review and assessment of USDA’s classified products;
Establish procedures to prevent unnecessary access to CNSI, including procedures that:
policy_statements.target: procedures to prevent unnecessary access to CNSI, including procedures that

policy_statements.source_text: Require a justification for access to CNSI before initiating security clearance procedures; and
Ensure that the number of persons granted access to CNSI is limited to the minimum consistent with operational and security requirements and needs.
Approve and inspect special contingency plans for the safeguarding of CNSI used in or near a high risk area;
policy_statements.target: of CNSI used in or near a high risk area

policy_statements.source_text: Through the Assistant Secretary of Administration (ASA) and the Director, Office of Human Resource Management (OHRM), ensure that applicable employee performance standards include language requiring the proper protection of CNSI for all employees who routinely handle such information.
For example, standards may include the statement, “Maintains classified national security information In Accordance With (IAW) E.O. 13526, Classified National Security Information and DM 3440-001.”
At a minimum, positions requiring this standard are:
Derivative classifiers;
Security specialists or ISCs, SSCs, TSCOs, SSOs; and
All other personnel whose duties significantly involve the creation or handling of CNSI.
Account for the costs associated with the implementation of E.O. 13526, which shall be reported annually to the Director of ISOO for publication;

Handle referrals for any request, appeal, challenge, complaint, or suggestion that pertains to CNSI that originated in a component of the Department that no longer exists, and for which there is no clear successor function;

Assist the OCA with the preparation of a Security Classification Guide (SCG) to facilitate the proper and uniform derivative classification and declassification of information (these guides shall conform to standards contained in directives issued under E.O. 13526);
Assist in establishing and implementing a program for systematic declassification reviews;

Ensure the safeguarding of foreign government information under standards that provide a degree of protection at least equivalent to that required by the providing government or international organization of governments that furnished the information;
policy_statements.target: safeguarding of foreign government information under standards that provide a degree of protection

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that USDA does not disclose information originally classified by another agency without its authorization;
Implement ISOO’s established classification and marking requirements for all CNSI handled, stored, and processed within USDA;
Ensure that North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) information is controlled and accounted for and all NATO security procedures are followed; and
Report to the SAO on the status of self-inspections and reporting yearly concurrent with the ISOO reporting requirements.
The ISC is the trusted agent representing OHSEC, PDSD and USDA to the Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices on matters relating to this DM.
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, Agencies, and Staff Offices

policy_statements.source_text: The ISC is the primary point of contact for security matters for their respective Agency and/or Staff Office.
policy_statements.target: Agency and/or Staff Office

policy_statements.source_text: The ISC is appointed in writing by their Agency Head that outlines their responsibilities and duties.
Duties include, but are not limited to:

Serve as the respective Mission Area, Agency, and Staff Office liaison for day-to-day security related activities and provide support for annual data calls, annual security refresher training, annual inspection of accredited spaces and equipment, and provide security assistance to their Agency, Mission Area, Staff Office on matters pertaining to accessing and/or handling CNSI;
policy_statements.target: support for annual data calls, annual security refresher training, annual inspection of accredited spaces and equipment

policy_statements.source_text: Possess a national security clearance commensurate to the level of information handled by the Mission Areas, Agency(s), and Staff Office(s) they represent as well as possess access to all approved facility(s) for which they are responsible;
Have thorough knowledge of their Mission Areas, Agency(s), and Staff Office(s) functions to include their classified missions or classified program support;
Have the ability to apply adequate resources to protect CNSI;
policy_statements.target: CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Initiate a preliminary inquiry when there is a failure to follow establish policy and procedures or there is suspicion of a possible compromise or loss of CNSI;
policy_statements.target: policy and procedures or there is suspicion of a possible compromise or loss of CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Immediately report security incidents, infractions and violations to the SSO;
policy_statements.target: security incidents, infractions and violations to the SSO

policy_statements.source_text: Provide to the SSO all requested information to meet requirements for annual reporting to ISOO;
Conduct inventories of classified assets and evaluating agency security needs, at a minimum on an annual basis;
policy_statements.target: inventories of classified assets and evaluating agency security needs, at a minimum on an annual basis

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate document reviews with the SSO for possible classification or declassification;
policy_statements.target: document reviews with the SSO for possible classification or declassification

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain a record management system in accordance with DR 3080-001, Records Management and the retention guide identified within this DM;
policy_statements.target: record management system

policy_statements.source_text: Review, comment on, and provide recommendations on draft security policy documents when requested by PDSD or OHSEC; and
policy_statements.target: recommendations on draft security policy documents

policy_statements.source_text: ISCs are responsible for designating an SSC.
policy_statements.target: SSC

policy_statements.source_text: ISCs shall collaborate with OHSEC to incorporate language defining security duties and responsibilities and qualifications for position descriptions and performance elements.
The SSC is responsible for assisting in many of the duties of the ISC as delegated by the ISC.
The SSC is the trusted agent representing PDSD and the ISC to the Secure Work Area (SWA).
policy_statements.target: Secure Work Area (SWA)

policy_statements.source_text: The SSC is the responsible person for all classified facilities that they have been appointed to oversee.
policy_statements.target: all classified facilities that they have been appointed to oversee

policy_statements.source_text: They are the day-to-day manager of those facilities to include the activities in those facilities.
policy_statements.target: those facilities

policy_statements.source_text: The SSC is appointed in writing by either their Agency Head or their ISC and report to the ISC for SWA matters.
Duties include, but are not limited to:

Serve as the official liaison between the ISC and the assigned SWA(s) for day-to-day security related activities and provide support for annual data calls, annual security refresher training, annual inspection of the accredited space(s) and equipment, and provide security assistance to all individuals with access to the SWA;
policy_statements.target: support for annual data calls, annual security refresher training, annual inspection of the accredited space(s) and equipment

policy_statements.source_text: Possess a national security clearance commensurate to the level of information stored, processed or handled in their assigned SWAs;
Conduct and record site specific training for all individuals on the access roster for their SWA, to include a review of the SWA Standard Operating Procedures (SOP);
Ensure that all visitors not on the access roster are signed in and have the appropriate clearance and identification before entering the space;
Have thorough knowledge of their Mission Areas, Agency(s), and Staff Office(s) functions to include their classified missions or classified program support;
Initiate a preliminary report when there is a failure to follow establish policy and procedures or there is suspicion of a possible compromise or loss of CNSI;
policy_statements.target: when there is a failure to follow establish policy and procedures or there is suspicion of a possible compromise or loss of CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Immediately report security violations and infractions to the ISC;
policy_statements.target: security violations and infractions to the ISC

policy_statements.source_text: Provide to the SSO and/or ISC all requested information to meet requirements for annual reporting to ISOO;
Conduct periodic inventories of classified assets and holdings;
policy_statements.target: periodic inventories of classified assets and holdings

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate document reviews with the ISC for consideration by SSO for possible classification or declassification;
policy_statements.target: document reviews with the ISC for consideration by SSO for possible classification or declassification

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain a record management system in accordance with DR 3080-001 and the retention guide identified within this DM; and
policy_statements.target: record management system

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure that all special or additional site specific measures, as identified in the SOP, are followed and documented as required.

The TSCO is the trusted agent representing OHSEC, PDSD and USDA in ensuring all that measures taken in matters relating to this DM to, track, record and store Top Secret material in their assigned Mission Areas, Agency(s), and Staff Office(s).
policy_statements.target: Mission Areas, Agency(s), and Staff Office(s)

policy_statements.source_text: They will assist with inventories of classified holdings and be able to report on status and disposition of Top Secret material.
They are also responsible for making sure that Top Secret classified material is kept to the minimum amount necessary and marked appropriately.
The TSCO reports directly to the Agency Head, or the ISC as prescribed on appointment.
The Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) has the responsibility to:
Certify and accredit USDA computer systems for processing collateral CNSI;
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)
policy_statements.target: USDA computer systems for processing collateral CNSI

policy_statements.source_text: Coordinate with PDSD, requests for processing collateral CNSI on USDA computers and establishing secure networks;
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)

policy_statements.source_text: Incorporate, where appropriate, applicable USDA information security policies and procedures into USDA policies and standards for Information Technology (IT) system protection.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)

policy_statements.source_text: System protection functions include communications security, encryption, network security products, and system reliability; and
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)

policy_statements.source_text: Identify cleared system administrators.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO)
policy_statements.target: cleared system administrators

policy_statements.source_text: USDA employees holding security clearances are required to:
Familiarize themselves with and adhering to the provisions of this DM;
Protect CNSI from individuals who do not have the appropriate clearance level as well as a need-to-know;
policy_statements.target: CNSI from individuals who do not have the appropriate clearance level as well as a need-to-know

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain the proper security clearance;
policy_statements.target: proper security clearance

policy_statements.source_text: Meet the accountability requirements identified within this DM;
Complete required security awareness and education training; and
policy_statements.target: required security awareness and education training

policy_statements.source_text: Report any security incidents immediately upon discovery to their respective SSC, ISC, or PDSD.
policy_statements.target: any security incidents immediately upon discovery to their respective SSC, ISC

policy_statements.source_text: Persons shall be allowed access to CNSI only if they:
Possess a valid and appropriate security investigation as stated in DR 4600-001, USDA Personnel Security Clearance Program;
cross_references: DR 4600-001, USDA Personnel Security Clearance Program

policy_statements.source_text: Have signed an accepted Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA); and
Have a valid need-to-know for the information in order to perform a lawful and authorized government function.
Special projects require program manager to authenticate material contribution for need-to-know.

In accordance with DR 4600-001, applicants for Top Secret, Secret and Confidential clearances may be granted an interim clearance provided there is no evidence of adverse information of material significance.
The interim clearance status will become a final clearance if results are favorable following completion of full investigative requirements.
Non United States (U.S.) citizens are not eligible for access to CNSI on an interim basis.
An interim Secret or Confidential clearance is valid for access to CNSI at the level of the eligibility granted, except for RD, Communication Security (COMSEC) Information, and NATO information.
An interim Top Secret clearance is valid for access to Top Secret information, RD, NATO Information, and COMSEC information at the Secret and Confidential level.

When an interim clearance has been granted and derogatory information is subsequently discovered or reported, the SSO will suspend access pending completion of the adjudication of the completed, final investigation.
conditions: When an interim clearance has been granted and derogatory information is subsequently discovered or reported

policy_statements.source_text: Suspension of access is not a denial or revocation of the clearance and may not be appealed.

Before being granted access to Confidential, Secret, or Top Secret information, employees must sign Standard Form (SF)-312, Classified Information Nondisclosure Agreement, or other NDA approved by the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI).
conditions: Before being granted access to Confidential

policy_statements.source_text: The SF-312 (or its predecessor, SF-189), or a legally enforceable facsimile retained in lieu of the original, shall be maintained for 50 years from the date of signature.
The original SF-312 will be maintained with the employee’s government Official Personnel File.
PDSD shall maintain a copy of the SF-312 for the duration of their access and a period of one (1) year from the date of their debriefing.
policy_statements.target: copy of the SF-312 for the duration of their access and a period of one (1) year from the date of their debriefing

policy_statements.source_text: Electronic signatures shall not be used to execute the SF-312.

Before being granted additional accesses, individuals adjudicated and approved will be required to sign any additional NDAs at the behest of the Cognizant Security Authority (CSA) and will be subject to any requirements therein.
conditions: Before being granted additional accesses

policy_statements.source_text: Individuals approved for access to SCI must sign Form 4414, Sensitive Compartmented Information Nondisclosure Agreement, and may be subject to a Counter Intelligence (CI) polygraph at the behest of the CSA.
policy_statements.actor_name: Individuals approved for access to SCI

policy_statements.source_text: This chapter establishes the policy and requirements for the Department’s SETA Program.

All individuals responsible for creating, processing, or handling CNSI for USDA must have a satisfactory knowledge of security policies, procedures, responsibilities, reporting, and classification management.
policy_statements.actor_name: All individuals responsible for creating, processing, or handling CNSI for USDA

policy_statements.source_text: E.O. 12968, Access to Classified Information, E.O. 13526, and E.O. 13587, and its implementing directives mandate that agencies conduct initial indoctrination training, mandatory annual refresher training, termination debriefings, and original and derivative classification training.
policy_statements.target: initial indoctrination training, mandatory annual refresher training, termination debriefings

policy_statements.source_text: All training must be documented, recorded and maintained in a central records management system for the duration of an individual’s access.
The SAO will ensure that all cleared employees receive accurate and relevant security training and briefings commensurate with their involvement with CNSI.
Specific and unique additional trainings will be identified by the SSO or the program manager relevant to the mission needs and environment.

The SAO will suspend classification authority of individuals who fail to complete mandatory training for original classification to include declassification or derivative classification in the required time and have not received a waiver.
policy_statements.target: mandatory training for original classification to include declassification or derivative classification in the required time and have not received a waiver

policy_statements.source_text: PDSD will conduct all security training via Aglearn.
policy_statements.target: all security training via Aglearn

policy_statements.source_text: Security training completed outside of Aglearn will be documented and updated in webSETS and or SIMS.
The SSO shall be responsible for ensuring that the ISCs complete all prescribed security training as outlined by PDSD and approved by the SAO.
policy_statements.target: all prescribed security training as outlined by PDSD and approved by the SAO

policy_statements.source_text: Training requirements shall be based on the agency’s or mission area’s involvement with CNSI.

Designated ISCs must display at a minimum; a general understanding of physical security, technical security, classification management, reporting, self-inspection, and personnel security disciplines that are applied in a CNSI program.
Acceptable training curriculums from ODNI, Office of the National Counterintelligence Executive or the Defense Security Service Academy are recommended.
ISCs shall be responsible for ensuring that designated SSCs have been appropriately trained.
Training requirements shall be based on the facility's involvement with CNSI and will include delegated authority, area familiarization, SOP, and self-inspection requirements/techniques.
All training will be documented by the ISC and forwarded to PDSD.
Initial briefings will be conducted either by the SSO or by a delegated ISC.
Prior to being granted access to CNSI, every employee shall receive an initial security briefing that includes, at a minimum, the following:
conditions: Prior to being granted access to CNSI
policy_statements.target: initial security briefing that includes, at a minimum, the following

policy_statements.source_text: Insider Threat awareness;
Operational security;
An overview of the security classification system (OCA and derivative);
Basic security policies, principles, practices;
Criminal, civil, and administrative penalties;
Employee reporting obligations and requirements;
Requirements for access and continued access;
Fraud Waste and Abuse (FWA) and whistleblower protection; and
Security procedures and duties applicable to USDA.
The SSC, in coordination with the ISC, shall prepare site specific training that details the procedures for the operational environment of their SWA.
Site specific training shall be conducted either by the ISC or SSC managing a facility.
The SSO shall provide site specific training for facilities under their direct control.
policy_statements.target: site specific training for facilities under their direct control

policy_statements.source_text: Site specific training will be completed and documented by the SSC’s on an annual basis.
The ISC will support the SAO’s requirement to ensure that all cleared employees receive security education and training at least annually.
At a minimum, the ISC will ensure their cleared employees complete the Departmental annual training, but may also provide supplemental training.
policy_statements.target: their cleared employees complete the Departmental annual training, but may also provide supplemental training

policy_statements.source_text: Refresher training will reinforce the information provided during the initial security briefing and will keep cleared employees informed of appropriate changes in security regulations.
Training methods may include group briefings, interactive videos, dissemination of instructional materials, or other media and methods.
All refresher training must be approved by PDSD.
The SSO will ensure that the SETA program meets the specific and unique requirements of the individual USDA programs.
ISCs shall maintain records about the programs offered and employee participation in them and forward all records to the SSOs or record them in a central database as specified by the SSO.
policy_statements.target: records about the programs offered and employee participation in them and forward all records to the SSOs or record them in a central database as specified by the SSO

policy_statements.source_text: The SSO or delegated ISC shall provide all cleared employees who are required to report their foreign travel, with security education and training regarding traveling Outside the Contiguous United States (OCONUS).
policy_statements.target: all cleared employees who are required to report their foreign travel, with security education and training regarding traveling Outside the Contiguous United States (OCONUS)

policy_statements.source_text: This training can be given on a case by case basis or to all cleared individuals at the discretion of the SSO or delegated ISC.
This training will include details about official or personal foreign travel and the risks to cleared individuals.
The training briefing will be approved by the SSO.

Once the briefing has been completed a cleared employee may travel to any low risk country (as determined by the SSO) with only a travel notification (using the Agriculture Department [AD]-1196, approved Foreign Travel Reporting Form).
conditions: Once the briefing has been completed a cleared employee may travel to any low risk country (as determined by the SSO) with only a travel notification (using the Agriculture Department [AD]-1196

policy_statements.source_text: This training will include a signed acknowledgement of responsibilities.
Upon return from the foreign travel, the individual must fill out and turn in the debriefing portion of the AD-1196 form within 10 business days.
conditions: Upon return from the foreign travel

policy_statements.source_text: The SSO will coordinate with the ISC to provide all cleared employees with some form of security education and training regarding traveling OCONUS to high risk countries/areas.
PDSD will maintain a current list of high risk countries.
policy_statements.target: current list of high risk countries

policy_statements.source_text: This training will include specific details about the risks of the intended destination to cleared individuals, to include current events, threats and risks.
The briefing will be conducted by the SSO or designee.
This training will include a signed acknowledgement of responsibilities.
Upon return from the foreign travel the individual must fill out and turn in the debriefing portion of the AD-1196 form within 10 business days.
The SSO or delegated ISC shall provide all cleared employees with a written foreign travel debriefing template or an in-person debriefing at the discretion of the SSO.
policy_statements.target: all cleared employees with a written foreign travel debriefing template or an in-person debriefing at the discretion of the SSO

policy_statements.source_text: All debriefings will be documented, recorded, maintained by the SSO, and forwarded to other agencies as required.

The SSO will ensure that the OCA at USDA has been adequately trained to perform their duties and is knowledgeable about the rules and regulations regarding the classification of new material and the creation of SCGs.

Individuals who fail to complete the annual training in proper classification and declassification will have their classification authority suspended until training is completed unless a waiver has been approved.
policy_statements.target: annual training in proper classification and declassification will have their classification authority suspended until training is completed

policy_statements.source_text: If waiver is approved, the employee will complete the training as soon as practicable.
conditions: If waiver is approved
policy_statements.target: training as soon as practicable

policy_statements.source_text: Upon the creation of an SCG all employees approved to use it for classification will be trained by the SSO or ISC in the proper use of SCGs and the proper creation of classified material.
This training will be completed yearly and include a signed acknowledgement of responsibilities.
Each classified activity shall have an SCG to identify Critical Program Information (CPI).

The SSO or delegated ISC shall provide designated cleared employees with a documented need to create derivatively classified material with training on the creation, marking, tracking and storage of derivative material.
policy_statements.target: designated cleared employees with a documented need to create derivatively classified material with training on the creation, marking, tracking and storage of derivative material

policy_statements.source_text: This training will be approved by the SSO, will be completed biennially and include a signed acknowledgement of responsibilities.
Employees who fail to complete derivative training will have their authority to apply derivative classification marking suspended until training is completed unless a waiver has been approved.
policy_statements.target: derivative training will have their authority to apply derivative classification marking suspended until training is completed

policy_statements.source_text: If waiver is approved, the employee will complete the training as soon as practicable.
conditions: If waiver is approved
policy_statements.target: training as soon as practicable

policy_statements.source_text: The SSO shall provide courier training to individuals who demonstrate a requirement to courier information.
policy_statements.target: courier training to individuals who demonstrate a requirement to courier information

policy_statements.source_text: There will be a generic briefing to qualify as a courier as well as specific training for couriers traveling OCONUS.
All instances of courier training will be documented by the SSO.
This training will be completed yearly and include a signed acknowledgement of responsibilities.

Prior to being granted access to classified SCI information, an employee shall receive an initial SCI security briefing that includes an overview of the security classification system of SCI material from the SSO as approved by the sponsor.
conditions: Prior to being granted access to classified SCI information
policy_statements.target: initial SCI security briefing that includes an overview of the security classification system of SCI material from the SSO as approved by the sponsor

policy_statements.source_text: After being granted access to classified SCI information, an employee shall receive an annual SCI security refresher training that includes an overview of the security classification system of SCI material from the SSO as approved by the sponsor.
conditions: After being granted access to classified SCI information
policy_statements.target: annual SCI security refresher training that includes an overview of the security classification system of SCI material from the SSO as approved by the sponsor

policy_statements.source_text: Prior to being granted access to an approved system for CNSI, an employee shall receive an initial training that includes an overview of the approved system, its requirements and extra training on marking electronic copies of CNSI as well as sending CNSI email and CNSI chats.
conditions: Prior to being granted access to an approved system for CNSI
policy_statements.target: initial training that includes an overview of the approved system, its requirements and extra training on marking electronic copies of CNSI as well as sending CNSI email and CNSI chats

policy_statements.source_text: This training must be approved by the SSO and recorded and documented by the ISCs and forwarded to the SSOs.

Employees who are unable to receive mandatory training in original classification, declassification or derivative classification marking in the required time due to an unavoidable circumstance will request in writing a waiver from the SAO.
policy_statements.target: mandatory training in original classification, declassification or derivative classification marking in the required time due to an unavoidable circumstance will request in writing a waiver from the SAO

policy_statements.source_text: The request will contain the following information:
Justification for the request; and
An expected time to complete the training.
policy_statements.target: training

policy_statements.source_text: A formal debriefing program must be developed and approved by the SSO and ISC.

SSOs or delegated ISCs shall formally debrief cleared employees at the time of termination of employment (discharge, resignation, or retirement), or when an employee's clearance is terminated, suspended, or revoked.
A formal debriefing should include at a minimum:
How to obtain a release before publishing;
What can and cannot be discussed or placed in resumes and applications for security clearances;
Turning in all holdings of CNSI;
Applicability of penalties for engaging in espionage;
Where to report suspected Foreign Intelligence Service (FIS) contacts or any attempted by unauthorized persons to solicit program data;
policy_statements.target: suspected Foreign Intelligence Service (FIS) contacts or any attempted by unauthorized persons to solicit program data

policy_statements.source_text: Appropriate espionage laws and codes; and
A NDA signed after the debriefing has taken place and forwarded to PDSD within two (2) business days.
In the event that an individual cannot be contacted, and the whereabouts of the individual cannot be determined within 30 days, the individual shall be administratively debriefed.
This process is to include the update of any applicable databases, as well as the signing of the SF-312 (using “administratively withdrawn” in place of the subject’s signature).
Classification is a process to determine if information can potentially cause damage to U.S. national security.
Classification includes many formal steps for which the OCA is trained.
Sometimes unclassified information combined or associated with other unclassified information may warrant classification.
This is referred to as classification by compilation or aggregation of information, and is often the larger picture that classifiers fail to see.
When it appears that an office has such an aggregation of information, the ISC should be contacted for assistance.
conditions: When it appears that an office has such an aggregation of information

policy_statements.source_text: A cleared subject matter expert must review the material and make an initial classification determination.
policy_statements.target: material and make an initial classification determination

policy_statements.source_text: If an agency ISC is not available, the SSO should be contacted for assistance.
conditions: If an agency ISC is not available

policy_statements.source_text: In some situations, an aggregation of CNSI may warrant a higher classification than its component parts.
For example, two (2) elements of information classified as Confidential may warrant a Secret classification when aggregated.
Below are the types of classification and what must be determined when classifying information.
policy_statements.target: information

policy_statements.source_text: The SSC, in coordination with their ISC, is responsible for maintaining a control system to account for the disposition of all USDA original and derivative materials, regardless of the classification level.
There are three (3) levels of classification:

CONFIDENTIAL – Shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause damage to the national security that the OCA is able to identify or describe;

SECRET – Shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause serious damage to the national security that the OCA is able to identify or describe; and

TOP SECRET – Shall be applied to information, the unauthorized disclosure of which reasonably could be expected to cause exceptionally grave damage to the national security that the OCA is able to identify or describe.
Original classification is the initial decision to designate a certain item of information as classified, at a certain level, and for a certain length of time.
An original classification decision can be made only by a U.S. Government official who has been designated or delegated the authority in writing.
The only USDA official with this authorization is the Secretary of Agriculture and may not be delegated.
A determination to originally classify information may be made only when:
policy_statements.target: information may be made only

policy_statements.source_text: An original classification authority is classifying the information;
policy_statements.target: information

policy_statements.source_text: The information falls into one or more of the categories set forth in Section 1.4 of E.O. 13526, as identified below:
Military plans, weapons systems, or operations;
Foreign government information;
Intelligence activities (including covert action), intelligence sources or methods, or cryptology;
Foreign relations or foreign activities of the U.S., including confidential sources;
Scientific, technological, or economic matters relating to the national security;
U.S. Government programs for safeguarding nuclear materials or facilities;
policy_statements.target: nuclear materials or facilities

policy_statements.source_text: Vulnerabilities or capabilities of systems, installations, infrastructures, projects, plans, or protection services relating to the national security; or
The development, production, or use of weapons of mass destruction.

The unauthorized disclosure of the information, either by itself or in context with other information, reasonably could be expected to cause damage to national security, which includes defense against transnational terrorism, that can be identified or described by the original classifier; and
The information is owned by, produced by or for, or is under the control of the U. S. Government.
The Secretary of Agriculture must state the concise “reason” for classification on the front of the document.

The original classifier must also indicate a date or event for the duration of classification up to 10 years from the date of the original classification unless the date is further extended due to information sensitivities for up to 25 years.
The date of origin of a classified document must be applied to OCA documents.

Derivative classification consists of the incorporating, paraphrasing, restating, or generating of a new form of information that has already been determined to be classified and marking the new material consistent with the classification markings of the source information.
This ensures that the new material is classified and handled at the level that the OCA has already determined.
As such, when classified information is incorporated, paraphrased, restated, or generated in new form, it will be marked with the classification markings that apply to the source information.
Derivative classification includes the classification of information based on guidance, which may be either a source document or classification guide.
The duplication or reproduction of existing CNSI is not derivative classification.
CNSI in email messages is subject to all requirements of E.O. 13526 and 32 CFR Part 2001, current editions.

If an email is transmitted on a classified system, or includes a classified attachment and contains no CNSI within the body of the email itself, then the email is not a derivative classification decision.
conditions: If an email is transmitted on a classified system

policy_statements.source_text: The email overall classification must reflect the highest level present in the attachment.
The Agency ISC shall ensure that all employees authorized to make derivative classification decisions:
Are identified by name and position, or by personal identifier, on documents they derivatively classify;
Observe and respect original classification decisions;
Carry forward the pertinent classification markings to any newly created documents.
For information derivatively classified based on multiple sources, the derivative classifier shall carry forward:
Both the date or event for declassification that corresponds to the longest period of classification among the sources;
A listing of the source materials.

Are trained, in accordance with SSO direction, in the proper application of the derivative classification principles, with an emphasis on avoiding over classification, at least once every two (2) years.

Training will cover classification levels, duration of classification, identification and markings, classification prohibitions and limitations, sanctions, classification challenges, security classification guides, and information sharing.
The training will be approved by the SSO;
Are given ready access to the pertinent classification guides and/or guidance necessary to fulfill these important actions; and
Whenever practicable, derivative classifiers shall use a classified addendum if CNSI constitutes a small portion of an otherwise unclassified document.
conditions: Whenever practicable

policy_statements.source_text: PDSD will establish a system for processing, tracking and recording formal classification challenges made by authorized holders.
policy_statements.target: system for processing, tracking and recording formal classification challenges made by authorized holders

policy_statements.source_text: Classification challenges shall be considered separately from Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) or other access requests, and shall not process such challenges in turn with pending access requests.
If an employee believes:
That information is classified improperly or unnecessarily;
That current security considerations justifies downgrading to a lower classification or upgrading to a higher classification; or
That the security classification guidance is improper or inadequate, the employee shall discuss such issues with the pertinent ISC or SSO for remedy.
If a solution is not forthcoming, and the employee believes that corrective action is still required, a formal written challenge shall be made to the ISC or SSO.
conditions: If a solution is not forthcoming

policy_statements.source_text: All challenges to classified information and/or material classifications shall be forwarded through the PDSD to the appropriate OCA.

Such challenges shall include a description sufficient to identify the issue, the reasons why the employee believes that corrective action is required, and any recommendations for appropriate corrective action.

Challengers and agencies shall attempt to keep all challenges, appeals and responses unclassified in any case; the information in question shall be safeguarded as required by this DM for its assigned or proposed level of classification, whichever is higher, until action is completed.
PDSD will provide a written response to the employee within 60 days.
policy_statements.target: written response to the employee within 60 days

policy_statements.source_text: If no written answer is received within 60 days from an external OCA, the SAO should be requested to provide assistance in obtaining a response or a date in which the response will be received.
conditions: If no written answer is received within 60 days from an external OCA
policy_statements.target: assistance in obtaining a response or a date in which the response will be received

policy_statements.source_text: If no response is received within 120 days, PDSD will notify the employee in writing of their right to forward the challenge to the Interagency Security Classification Appeals Panel (ISCAP).
conditions: If no response is received within 120 days

policy_statements.source_text: The employee may also forward the challenge to the ISCAP if an agency has not responded to an internal appeal within 90 days of the agency’s receipt of the appeal.
The fact that an employee has initiated such a challenge will not, in any way, serve as a basis for adverse action by the Government.
If an employee believes that adverse action did result from a classification challenge, full details should be furnished promptly to the ISOO for resolution.
conditions: If an employee believes that adverse action did result from a classification challenge

policy_statements.source_text: Whenever an employee originates information they believe should be classified the following rules shall apply:
If the information was previously identified as classified, it shall be classified according to an appropriate SCG or source document, and marked as required by this DM.
conditions: If the information was previously identified as classified

policy_statements.source_text: If the information was not previously classified, but the employee believes the information may or should be classified, the employee should protect the information as though classified at the appropriate level and submit it to the agency that has an interest in the subject matter for a classification determination.
conditions: If the information was not previously classified
policy_statements.target: information as though classified at the appropriate level and submit it to the agency that has an interest in the subject matter for a classification determination

policy_statements.source_text: In such a case, the following marking, or one that clearly conveys the same meaning, may be used:
CLASSIFICATION DETERMINATION PENDING
Protect as though classified (Top Secret, Secret, or Confidential)
policy_statements.target: as though classified (Top Secret, Secret

policy_statements.source_text: This marking shall appear conspicuously at least once on the material but no further markings are necessary until a classification determination is received.
In addition, employees are not precluded from marking such material as SSI, or any other information control structure enacted at USDA for the protection of unclassified information.
Pending a final classification determination by the OCA, the employee should protect the information.
conditions: Pending a final classification determination by the OCA
policy_statements.target: information

policy_statements.source_text: It should be noted however, that E.O. 13526 prohibits classification of information over which the Government has no jurisdiction.
The fact that CNSI has been made public does not mean that it is automatically declassified.
Employees shall continue the classification until formally advised to the contrary.
Questions about the propriety of continued classification in these cases should be brought to the immediate attention of the SSC, ISC or SSO.
Information is downgraded or declassified based on the loss of sensitivity of the information due to the passage of time or on occurrence of a specific event.
Only an SSO or delegated ISC can downgrade or declassify information based on formal notification from the OCA.
policy_statements.target: information based on formal notification from the OCA

policy_statements.source_text: If material is marked for automatic declassification, the employee shall seek guidance from the SSO or ISC prior to taking any action.
conditions: If material is marked for automatic declassification

policy_statements.source_text: The SSO will coordinate with the subject matter expert a justification for an exemption from the automatic declassification requirement.
The SSO will prepare the notification from the SAO to the Director of ISOO with specific information being proposed for exemption from automatic declassification.
The notification will be submitted to the Director of ISOO at least one (1) year before the information is subject to automatic declassification and the notification will include:
A detailed description of the information, either by reference to information in specific records or in the form of a declassification guide;
An explanation of why the information should be exempt from automatic declassification and must remain classified for a longer period of time; and
A specific date or a specific and independently verifiable event for automatic declassification of specific records that contain the information proposed for exemption.

After a review of specific series of records as defined in section 6.1(r) of E.O. 13526, it is determined that the series of records almost invariable contain information that falls within one (1) of more of the exemption categories under section 3.3(b) of E.O. 13526, the SAO will submit the request for exemption to the Director of ISOO at least one (1) year prior to the onset of automatic declassification.
conditions: After a review of specific series of records as defined in section 6.1(r) of E.O. 13526
policy_statements.target: of specific series of records as defined in section 6

policy_statements.source_text: Copies of records within the specific file series or records of a similar topic to the specific files series located elsewhere may be exempted in accordance with exemptions approved by the ISCAP.
Downgrading or declassifying actions constitute implementation of a directed action rather than an exercise of the authority for deciding the change or cancellation of the classification.
At the time the material is actually downgraded or declassified, the action to update records and change the classification markings shall be initiated and performed by the SSO or ISC.
Declassification is not an automatic approval for public disclosure.
Physically marking CNSI with appropriate classification markings serves to warn and inform holders of the information of the degree of protection required.
Other notations facilitate downgrading, declassification, and aid in derivative classification actions.

Therefore, it is essential that all CNSI be marked to clearly convey to the holder the level of classification assigned, the portions that contain or reveal CNSI, the period of time protection is required, the identity (by name and position or personal identifier) of the classifier, the source(s) for derivative classification, and any other notations required for protection of the information.
All classified material shall be marked and controlled in accordance with the ISOO marking guide, the program SCG, and other program guidance.
As a general rule, the markings specified in paragraphs c through h below are required for all CNSI regardless of the form in which it appears.
Some material, such as documents, letters, and reports, can be easily marked with the required markings.
Marking other material, such as equipment, Information Systems media, and slides may be more difficult due to size or other physical characteristics.

Since the primary purpose of the markings is to alert the holder that the information requires special protection, it is essential that all classified material be marked to the fullest extent possible to ensure the necessary safeguarding.
policy_statements.target: necessary safeguarding

policy_statements.source_text: All classified material shall be marked to show the name and address of the employee responsible for its preparation, the identity of the person (by name and position or personal identifier) responsible for each derivative classification action, and the date of preparation.
These markings are required on the face of all classified documents.
The highest level of CNSI contained in a document is its overall marking.
The overall marking shall be conspicuously marked or stamped at the top and bottom on the outside of the front cover, on the title page, on the first page, and on the outside of the back.
All copies of classified documents shall also bear the required markings.

Overall markings shall be stamped, printed, etched, written, engraved, painted, or affixed by means of a tag, sticker, decal, or similar device on classified material other than documents, and on containers of such material, if possible.
If marking the material or container is not practical, written notification of the markings shall be furnished to recipients.
conditions: If marking the material or container is not practical

policy_statements.source_text: Top Secret notebooks are to be permanently bound documents with each page numbered consecutively, front and back.

Interior pages of classified documents shall be conspicuously marked or stamped at the top and bottom with the highest classification of the information appearing thereon, or the designation UNCLASSIFIED, if all the information on the particular page is UNCLASSIFIED.

Alternatively, the overall classification of the document may be conspicuously marked or stamped at the top and bottom of each interior page, when necessary to achieve production efficiency, and the particular information to which classification is assigned is adequately identified by portion markings according to subsection f below.
The major components of complex documents are likely to be used separately.
In such cases, each major component shall be marked as a separate document.
Examples include:
Each annex, appendix, or similar component of a plan, program, or project description;
Attachments and appendices to a letter; and
Each major part of a report.

If an entire major component is UNCLASSIFIED, the first page of the component may be marked at the top and bottom with the designation UNCLASSIFIED and a statement included, such as: All portions of this (annex, appendix, etc.) are UNCLASSIFIED.
conditions: If an entire major component is UNCLASSIFIED

policy_statements.source_text: When this method of marking is used, no further markings are required on the unclassified major component.
conditions: When this method of marking is used

policy_statements.source_text: Each section, part, paragraph, or similar portion of a document containing CNSI shall be marked to show the highest level of its classification, or that the portion is unclassified.
Portions of documents shall be marked in a manner that eliminates doubt as to which of its portions contain or reveal CNSI.
Classification levels of portions of a document shall be shown by the appropriate classification symbol placed immediately before the portion to which it applies.
For paragraphs or subparagraphs beginning with numbers, letters or symbols such as bullets, place the portion marking after the number, letter or bullet and before the text.
In marking portions, the parenthetical symbols (TS) for Top Secret, (S) for Secret, (C) for Confidential, and (U) for Unclassified shall be used.
Illustrations, photographs, figures, graphs, drawings, charts, or similar portions contained in classified documents shall be marked clearly to show their classified or unclassified status.
These classification markings shall not be abbreviated and shall be prominent and placed within or contiguous to such a portion.
Captions of such portions shall be marked on the basis of their content.
Unclassified subjects and titles shall be selected for classified documents, if possible.
A subject or title shall be marked with the appropriate symbol placed immediately before the item, which shall reflect the classification of the title, not the content of the document.
All CNSI shall be marked to reflect the source of the classification and declassification instructions.
Documents shall show the required information either on the cover, first page, title page, or in another prominent position.
Other material shall show the required information on the material itself or, if not practical, in related or accompanying documentation.
The purpose of the “Classified By” line is to identify the person who applies derivative classification markings for the document.
If not otherwise evident, the agency and office of origin will be identified and follow the name and position or personal identifier of the derivative classifier.
conditions: If not otherwise evident

policy_statements.source_text: The purpose of the "Derived From" line is to link the derivative classification applied to the material by the employee and the source document(s) or classification guide(s) under which it was classified.
